quotes.quote: Serum 25(OH)D levels were compared between groups using the independent t test and within the same group using paired t test. Categorical variables (proportions) were compared using Pearson
chi-squared test or Fisher’s exact test, as applicable. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used for comparison between different seasons.

specification.exact_target: Mean serum 25(OH)D level at 12 months in the low dose (600 IU/day) and high dose (3750 IU/day) vitamin D3 arms: 26.0 ng/mL and 36.0 ng/mL, respectively.
specification.blind_target: Mean serum 25(OH)D level at 12 months in the low dose and high dose vitamin D3 arms.
specification.target_location: Abstract Results; also reported in Results section 'Response to Vitamin D3 Supplementation'.

location_quotes.quote: Results Mean 25(OH)D level at 12 months was 26.0
ng/mL with low dose and 36.0 ng/mL with high dose vitamin D 3 .

The mean 25(OH)D levels reached after 12 months were 26.0 ± 6.9 ng/mL in the low dose arm and 36.0 ± 9.7 ng/mL in the high dose arm ( P < 0.001), both of which did not differ significantly between genders (Supplement 1) ( 21 ).

method_quotes.quote: Serum 25(OH)D levels were compared between groups using the independent t test and within the same group using paired t test.
Serum 25(OH)D was run using liquid chromatography mass spectroscopy (LCMS) at the Mayo Clinic Clinical Laboratories, (Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota).
